candidates.exact_span: The discharge from the facility is to Lower Animas Ditch, an irrigation facility with return flows at various locations, including diversions to Hampton Arroyo and Williams Arroyo, subject to Section 20.6.4.98 New Mexico Administrative Code (NMAC) (if non-perennial) and Section 20.6.4.99 NMAC (if perennial)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the receiving ditch is treated as perennial or non-perennial, and whether return-flow routing through Hampton or Williams Arroyo governs, changes which NMAC segment provisions and water-quality criteria are selected for limit comparison (A) and may change segment-conditional monitoring applicability (B).

candidates.exact_span: then Animas River, from Estes Arroyo upstream to the Southern Ute Indian Tribal boundary, a classified segment described in Section 20.6.4.404 NMAC and from the confluence with the San Juan River upstream to Estes Arroyo, a classified segment described in Section 20.6.4.403 NMAC; then San Juan River, a classified segment described from the Navajo Nation Boundary at Hogback to Animas River in Section 20.6.4.401 NMAC in the San Juan River Basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which classified segment(s) are the legally relevant receiving water for Outfall 001 would change which segment-specific numeric standards are used when selecting enforceable discharge limits.

candidates.exact_span: The general and specific stream standards are provided in "New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Waters," (20.6.4 NMAC, effective as of May 22, 2020 for purposes of State implementation and approved by EPA for Clean Water Act Purposes on July 24, 2020).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which 20.6.4 NMAC edition or approval status controls FY2025 compliance could change the numeric criteria applied when comparing reported measurements to limits.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of all non-perennial surface waters of the state, except those ephemeral waters included under Section 20.6.4.97 NMAC or classified in Sections 20.6.4.101-899 NMAC are livestock watering, wildlife habitat, marginal warmwater aquatic life and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the discharge path is read as non-perennial, the assigned designated uses (and exceptions for ephemeral or specially classified waters) determine which use-protective criteria feed into applicable numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses in all perennial surface waters of the state except those classified in Sections 20.6.4.101-899 NMAC are warmwater aquatic life, livestock watering, wildlife habitat and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the discharge path is read as perennial but not covered by a special classification, these default designated uses would drive a different criteria set than the Animas River-specific uses below.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of Animas River, in both Section 20.6.4.403 and 404 NMAC, are coolwater aquatic life, irrigation, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, public water supply, industrial water supply and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Site-specific Animas River designated uses (including coolwater aquatic life and irrigation) override general perennial defaults and can change which numeric criteria are selected for limit comparison.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Table I figures are treated as enforceable permit limits or as pre-permit characterization from application materials changes whether numeric compliance comparisons are performed (A); the cited application dates may also bear on which permit version or renewal governs FY2025 monitoring obligations (B).

The Max and Avg columns may be read as enforceable effluent limits for flow; different interpretations of whether max, average, or both apply would change exceedance determinations for reported flow measurements.

Numeric Max/Avg values for TSS may be treated as enforceable discharge limits; ambiguity over which column governs compliance would change whether reported TSS is compared against 19 mg/l, 4.55 mg/l, or both.

The parenthetical "(from DMR)" may indicate report-only DMR tracking rather than an enforceable effluent limit (A), may establish an expectation that TDS be reported on DMRs (B), and affects how missing or DMR-only TDS evidence is classified when no ordinary numeric result is available (C).

pH is expressed with both a maximum and minimum; different readings of how these bounds operate as enforceable limits would change whether a reported pH value is treated as exceeding an applicable limit.
